top_signal.title: Health insurance options for small business owners
top_signal.summary: My husband and I both own our own small businesses, and we’re struggling to figure out what to do for health insurance. We make too much to qualify for Marketplace subsidies, but paying full price for traditional health insurance is outrageously expensive and honestly doesn’t feel financially realistic for us.  We’re both healthy, rarely go to the doctor, and have a young child, with hopes of having one more in the future.   Ideally, we’re looking for something that:   Provides coverage for major medical emergencies — cancer, serious accidents, unexpected surgeries, hospitalizations, etc. Our biggest concern is protecting ourselves financially if something catastrophic happens.   Is HSA-eligible. Having the ability to contribute to an HSA is really important to us, especially for the tax advantages as two self-employed individuals.   Has affordable monthly premiums. We’re comfortable paying out of pocket for routine appointments and smaller medical expenses. We don’t need a plan with low copays or extensive everyday benefits.   Offers some peace of mind without costing us an arm and a leg every month.   It feels like we’re stuck in that frustrating middle ground where we make too much to receive financial assistance but not enough to comfortably afford the full cost of family health insurance.   I’m sure there are plenty of other self-employed families in this exact situation, so I’d love to hear what everyone else is doing. Thanks so much        submitted by     /u/a
